name: English
title: Africa Atlas
sub: Open dataset on all 54 African countries (JSON): population by gender, GDP, PPP GDP, languages, currency and time zones, ready for data analysis.
missing: Tip not translated yet: contribute on GitHub!
foot: Rounded, approximate figures (2024 orders of magnitude). GDP in USD billions, PPP GDP in international dollars. 'Languages' = living languages recorded. Western Sahara and Somaliland are not listed separately. Check official travel advisories before you go. Data CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

tips.dz: Visa required. The dinar can't be exported and foreign cards are rarely accepted: bring cash.
tips.eg: Haggle for taxis and bazaar goods; 'baksheesh' (small tips) is customary. Avoid the July–August heat.
tips.ly: Most governments advise against travel: check official advisories first.
tips.ma: Bargain in the souks. The dirham can't be exported. Hours change during Ramadan.
tips.sd: Armed conflict: travel strongly discouraged; check official advisories.
tips.tn: Pay in cash outside hotels. Best seasons: March–May and October.
tips.bj: Porto-Novo is the capital but Cotonou is the economic hub. Yellow fever vaccine required; zem (motorbike taxis) everywhere. Voodoo Festival on 10 January in Ouidah.
tips.bf: Border areas are risky: follow official advisories. The FESPACO film festival is held in Ouagadougou in odd-numbered years.
tips.cv: Few flights and ferries link the islands: leave a buffer. Morna music and Cesária Évora in Mindelo.
tips.ci: Abidjan is the real metropolis. 'Maquis' are popular open-air restaurants; mobile money is widespread.
tips.gm: Smallest mainland African country. Banjul–Barra ferry. Dry season: November–May.
tips.gh: Use your right hand to greet and eat. Tro-tro minibuses are very cheap.
tips.gn: Frequent power cuts and heavy traffic in Conakry. Heavy rains June–September.
tips.gw: Bijagós archipelago (biosphere reserve). Few ATMs: bring cash.
tips.lr: US dollars are accepted everywhere. Roads are very poor in the rainy season.
tips.ml: North and centre not advised. Bamako: markets and music; harmattan dust December–February.
tips.mr: Alcohol is banned. Friday is the rest day. The iron-ore train from Choum is among the longest in the world.
tips.ne: Agadez is UNESCO-listed; outside Niamey, follow official advisories. Extreme heat April–June.
tips.ng: Africa's most populous country, 500+ languages. In Lagos, allow hours for traffic.
tips.sn: Agree taxi fares before getting in. Gorée Island is 20 minutes by boat. Local hospitality is called 'teranga'.
tips.sl: Superb beaches near Freetown. Heavy rains May–October.
tips.tg: Lomé sits right on the Ghana border. Cheap zem rides. Big Assigamé market.
tips.ao: Luanda is among the world's most expensive cities. Portuguese is official.
tips.cm: 'Africa in miniature' (volcanoes, savanna, coast). Tensions in anglophone regions: check advisories.
tips.cf: Unstable security: travel discouraged outside authorised zones.
tips.td: Permit required to take photos. Lake Chad area is risky. Sahel, Sahara and savanna cultures.
tips.cg: Brazzaville and Kinshasa face each other across the river: the two closest capitals in the world.
tips.cd: Mountain gorillas in Virunga. East: check advisories. Yellow fever vaccine required.
tips.gq: Only African country with Spanish as an official language. Visa hard to get. Malabo is on Bioko island.
tips.ga: About 88% of the land is forest. Loango Park: elephants and hippos on the beach.
tips.st: Excellent chocolate and coffee. Few flights: book early. Best season June–September.
tips.bi: Gitega is the political capital, Bujumbura the economic one. Lake Tanganyika.
tips.km: Karthala volcano is still active. Few ferries and flights between islands.
tips.dj: Lake Assal lies 155 m below sea level. Stifling heat May–September; whale shark diving.
tips.er: Asmara is UNESCO-listed (modernist architecture). Permits needed to leave the city. Foreign cards don't work in ATMs.
tips.et: 13-month calendar, 7–8 years behind ours; hours are counted from sunrise.
tips.ke: Masai Mara migration July–October. M-Pesa payments everywhere. Electronic authorisation (eTA) required.
tips.mg: Slow roads: allow extra time. Respect 'fady' (local taboos). Baobabs at Morondava.
tips.mw: Nicknamed 'the warm heart of Africa'. Lake Malawi holds 700+ fish species.
tips.mu: Drive on the left. Very safe. Creole is the everyday language; English and French are official.
tips.mz: North (Cabo Delgado) not advised. Beaches of Tofo and Vilanculos. Portuguese is official.
tips.rw: Plastic bags banned. Last Saturday of the month: 'Umuganda' community clean-up. Gorilla permits are pricey.
tips.sc: Expensive destination, book early. Vallée de Mai (coco de mer palm) is UNESCO-listed.
tips.so: Travel discouraged. Mobile money dominates: most payments are digital.
tips.ss: World's youngest country (2011). Unstable: official advisories essential.
tips.tz: Dodoma is the capital, Dar es Salaam the largest city. Kilimanjaro, Serengeti, Zanzibar.
tips.ug: Boda-bodas (motorbike taxis) everywhere. Bwindi gorilla permits sell out: book far ahead.
tips.bw: Okavango Delta. 'Pula' means both 'rain' and 'luck'. Drive on the left.
tips.sz: Africa's last absolute monarchy. Umhlanga Reed Dance in August–September.
tips.ls: Landlocked inside South Africa; the lowest point is above 1,400 m. Pack warm clothes.
tips.na: Huge distances, gravel roads. Namib Desert and Sossusvlei. Drive on the left.
tips.za: Three capitals (Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein). 12 official languages. Power cuts possible. Take care at night.
tips.zm: Victoria Falls from the Zambian side. Walking safaris in Luangwa Valley.
tips.zw: US dollars widely used. Victoria Falls and Hwange. Carry cash.
